source: Código Limpo (Robert C. Martin), ch. 17 'Odores e Heurísticas' (Smells and Heuristics), PDF p.280-309
notes: page = PDF page where the heuristic starts. title = the title printed in the Brazilian Portuguese edition; title_en = English title (the usual English wording of the heuristic). related = links inferred from the text (not a list from the book), except when the book itself cites the code. detectable='script' = a simple syntactic heuristic can flag candidates; the final decision is always judgment ('julgamento' = requires reviewer judgment).

smells.title: Informações inapropriadas
smells.summary: A comment holding change history, author, date or ticket number; that belongs in version control or the issue tracker. Comments should deal only with technical information about the code and design.

smells.title: Comentário obsoleto
smells.summary: An old, irrelevant or incorrect comment that has drifted from the code and now misleads. Update it or delete it right away; better still, do not write comments that are bound to age.

smells.title: Comentários redundantes
smells.summary: A comment that repeats what the code already says by itself (e.g. a Javadoc that only repeats the signature). Comment only what the code cannot express.

smells.title: Comentário mal escrito
smells.summary: If a comment is worth writing, write it with care: well-chosen words, correct grammar and punctuation, no stating the obvious, brief.

smells.title: Código como comentário
smells.summary: Commented-out code rots, confuses, and nobody dares delete it. Delete it: version control keeps the history.

smells.title: Construir requer mais de uma etapa
smells.title_en: Build Requires More Than One Step
smells.summary: Building the project should be a single, simple operation: get the code with one command and build it with another, with no arcane scripts or hunting for dependencies.

smells.title: Testes requerem mais de uma etapa
smells.title_en: Tests Require More Than One Step
smells.summary: You should be able to run all the unit tests with a single command (or an IDE button); running everything must be quick, easy and obvious.

smells.title: Parâmetros em excesso
smells.summary: Functions should have few arguments: zero is best, then one, two and three; more than three is questionable and should be avoided.

smells.title: Parâmetros de saída
smells.summary: Readers expect input arguments, not output ones. If the function must change state, let it change the state of the object it is called on.

smells.title: Parâmetros lógicos
smells.summary: A boolean argument announces that the function does more than one thing and confuses whoever reads the call; eliminate it by splitting the function.

smells.title: Função morta
smells.summary: Methods that are never called should be discarded; version control remembers them if needed.

smells.title: Múltiplas linguagens em um arquivo fonte
smells.title_en: Multiple Languages in One Source File
smells.summary: Mixing several languages (XML, HTML, JavaScript, Java, tags) in one file is confusing. The ideal is one language per file; in practice, minimize the number and extent of the extra languages.

smells.title: Comportamento óbvio não é implementado
smells.summary: By the Principle of Least Surprise, a function or class should do what another programmer would expect from its name (e.g. accept abbreviations and ignore case when converting a day name). Without that, the reader loses trust and must read every detail.

smells.title: Comportamento incorreto nos limites
smells.summary: Do not trust the intuition that the code works: handle every boundary condition, corner case and exception, and write a test for each.

smells.title: Seguranças anuladas
smells.summary: Turning off compiler warnings, controls such as serialVersionUID, or failing tests, promising to fix it later, is risky and costly in debugging.

smells.title: Duplicação
smells.summary: One of the most important rules in the book (DRY / 'once and only once'). Every duplication is a missed abstraction: extract methods for identical blocks, use polymorphism for repeated switch/if, and Template Method or Strategy for similar algorithms.

smells.title: Códigos no nível errado de abstração
smells.title_en: Code at Wrong Level of Abstraction
smells.summary: High-level concepts and low-level details must live in separate containers (base class vs. derived classes, modules, components). Example: percentFull does not belong to every Stack, but to a BoundedStack.

smells.title: As classes base dependem de suas derivadas
smells.title_en: Base Classes Depending on Their Derivatives
smells.summary: A base class that knows the names of its derivatives signals a problem; the base should not see its derivatives, so they can be deployed in separate jars/components. Exception: a fixed number of derivatives, as in finite state machines.

smells.title: Informações excessivas
smells.summary: Module interfaces should be small: few methods, few variables, few protected members. Hide data, utilities, constants and temporaries to keep coupling low.

smells.title: Código morto
smells.summary: Code that never executes (an impossible if, a catch that cannot occur, an uncalled utility, an unreachable case) ages and smells bad. Delete it.

smells.title: Separação vertical
smells.summary: Declare local variables just above their first use and private functions just below their first use, minimizing vertical distance.

smells.title: Inconsistência
smells.summary: Do similar things the same way: the same variable name for the same kind of object, parallel names for parallel methods. Choose conventions and follow them.

smells.title: Entulho
smells.summary: Empty constructors, unused variables, functions never called and comments with no information are clutter: remove them.

smells.title: Acoplamento artificial
smells.summary: Independent things should not be coupled for convenience (e.g. a general enum inside a specific class, a general static function in a specific class). Decide carefully where to declare each element.

smells.title: Feature Envy
smells.summary: A method that manipulates another object's data through getters/setters 'envies' that class and perhaps should live in it. Sometimes it is a necessary evil (e.g. formatting a report without coupling the model to the format).

smells.title: Parâmetros seletores
smells.summary: An argument (boolean, enum, integer) that chooses the behavior merges several functions into one. Prefer several functions to passing a selector code.

smells.title: Propósito obscuro
smells.summary: Chained expressions, Hungarian notation and magic numbers hide intent. It is worth the time to make the purpose visible to the reader.

smells.title: Responsabilidade mal posicionada
smells.summary: Put code where the reader expects it (principle of least surprise): PI next to the trigonometric functions, totals computed in the function whose name says so. If you move it for performance, the names must reflect that.

smells.title: Modo estático inadequado
smells.summary: Static is appropriate when all the data comes from the arguments and there is no chance of polymorphism (Math.max). When in doubt, prefer a non-static method.

smells.title: Use variáveis descritivas
smells.summary: Break calculations into intermediate values held in variables with explanatory names; more explanatory variables is generally better.

smells.title: Nomes de funções devem dizer o que elas fazem
smells.title_en: Function Names Should Say What They Do
smells.summary: If you must look at the implementation or the documentation to know what the function does (e.g. date.add(5)), choose a better name or reorganize the functionality.

smells.title: Entenda o algoritmo
smells.summary: Passing the tests is not enough: understand why the solution is correct. The best way is usually to refactor until it is obvious that it works.

smells.title: Torne dependências lógicas em físicas
smells.summary: A dependent module should not assume things about the other (logical dependency); it should ask explicitly for what it needs. E.g. instead of a PAGE_SIZE constant in the reporter, ask the formatter getMaxPageSize().

smells.title: Prefira polimorfismo a if...else ou switch...case
smells.title_en: Prefer Polymorphism to If/Else or Switch/Case
smells.summary: Consider polymorphism before a switch; functions are rarely more volatile than types. The ONE SWITCH rule: at most one switch per type of selection, and it must create polymorphic objects.
smells.title_note: The OCR reads 'if...e/se'; the image (p.294) shows 'if...else ou switch...case'.

smells.title: Siga as convenções padrões
smells.summary: The team should follow a coding standard based on industry norms (names, brace placement, where to declare variables); the code itself serves as the example, with no document needed.

smells.title: Substitua os números mágicos por constantes com nomes
smells.title_en: Replace Magic Numbers with Named Constants
smells.summary: Loose numbers should become well-named constants (86400 -> SECONDS_PER_DAY). Exceptions: self-explanatory formulas and very well-known values; 'magic number' applies to any token with no evident meaning, including strings.

smells.title: Seja preciso
smells.summary: Decisions in the code must be precise: check for null when the function may return it, do not use floating point for money, handle concurrency and queries that may return more than one record, declare List instead of ArrayList when that is enough.

smells.title: Estrutura acima de convenção
smells.summary: Prefer decisions enforced by structure to those based on convention: a base class with abstract methods forces implementation; a switch over well-named enums does not.

smells.title: Encapsule as condicionais
smells.summary: Boolean logic inside if/while is hard to read; extract a function whose name explains the intent (shouldBeDeleted(timer)).

smells.title: Evite condicionais negativas
smells.summary: Negative conditions are harder to understand; whenever possible use the positive form (shouldCompact instead of !shouldNotCompact).

smells.title: As funções devem fazer uma coisa só
smells.summary: Functions with several sections that perform a series of operations should be split into smaller functions that each do one thing.

smells.title: Acoplamentos temporários ocultos
smells.summary: If the call order matters, make it explicit: each function produces the result that the next one receives as an argument (bucket brigade), making the wrong order impossible.

smells.title: Não seja arbitrário
smells.summary: Have a reason for the structure of the code and make it visible; arbitrary structure invites changes. E.g. a public nested class with no need, used by unrelated classes.

smells.title: Encapsule as condições de limites
smells.summary: Concentrate boundary handling in one place; avoid scattered +1 and -1 (e.g. a repeated level + 1 becomes nextLevel).

smells.title: Funções devem descer apenas um nível de
smells.title_en: Functions Should Descend Only One Level of Abstraction
smells.summary: All statements of a function should be at the same level of abstraction, one below the operation the name describes. E.g. a render that mixes the concept of a horizontal rule with the syntax of the HR tag.
smells.title_note: Truncated printed title: the word 'abstração' is missing in the Brazilian edition (the same happens in the body text). Checked against the image of p.299.

smells.title: Mantenha os dados configuráveis em níveis altos
smells.title_en: Keep Configurable Data at High Levels
smells.summary: Configuration constants and known default values at a high level should not be buried in low-level functions; expose them at the top and pass them down as arguments.

smells.title: Evite a navegação transitiva
smells.summary: Modules should know only their immediate collaborators (Law of Demeter, 'shy code'); avoid a.getB().getC().doSomething(), which makes the architecture rigid.

smells.title: Evite longas listas de importação usando wildcards (caracteres curinga)
smells.title_en: Avoid Long Import Lists by Using Wildcards
smells.summary: When using two or more classes from a package, import the package with a wildcard; long lists are intimidating and specific imports are hard dependencies. Name conflicts are rare and manageable.

smells.title: Não herde as constantes
smells.summary: Do not implement an interface just to gain access to its constants; this hides the origin at the top of the hierarchy. Use static import.

smells.title: Constantes versus enum
smells.summary: Use enum (since Java 5) instead of public static final int; enums have names, methods and fields, giving more expressiveness.

smells.title: Escolha nomes descritivos
smells.summary: Choose names carefully and reevaluate them as the software evolves; the book states that names are 90% responsible for readability.

smells.title: Escolha nomes no nível apropriado de abstração
smells.title_en: Choose Names at the Appropriate Level of Abstraction
smells.summary: Names should reflect the level of abstraction of the class or function, not the implementation. E.g. Modem.dial(phoneNumber) becomes connect(connectionLocator).

smells.title: Use uma nomenclatura padrão onde for possível
smells.summary: Use existing conventions: the design pattern name in the class (AutoHangupModemDecorator), toString in Java, and the project's ubiquitous language (Eric Evans).

smells.title: Nomes não ambíguos
smells.summary: The name must not leave the task of the function or variable ambiguous; e.g. doRename becomes renamePageAndOptionallyAllReferences, even if long.

smells.title: Use nomes longos para escopos grandes
smells.title_en: Use Long Names for Long Scopes
smells.summary: The length of the name should follow the scope: i and j are fine in loops of a few lines; the larger the scope, the longer and more precise the name.

smells.title: Evite codificações
smells.summary: Do not encode type or scope in the name (prefixes m_, f, siv_); IDEs already provide that information. Avoid Hungarian pollution.

smells.title: Nomes devem descrever os efeitos colaterais
smells.summary: The name must tell everything the function does, including side effects; a getOos that creates the object if it does not exist should be createOrReturnOos.

smells.title: Testes insuficientes
smells.summary: The suite should test everything that can fail; while there are unexplored conditions or unvalidated calculations, the tests are insufficient ('looks good' is not a criterion).

smells.title: Use uma ferramenta de cobertura!
smells.summary: Coverage tools show gaps in the testing strategy, highlighting ifs and catches whose bodies were not exercised.

smells.title: Não pule testes triviais
smells.summary: Trivial tests are cheap and are worth more as documentation than they cost.

smells.title: Um teste ignorado é uma questão sobre uma ambiguidade
smells.title_en: An Ignored Test Is a Question about an Ambiguity
smells.summary: When the requirement is unclear, record the doubt as a commented-out test or one annotated with @Ignore, depending on whether the ambiguity compiles or not.

smells.title: Teste as condições de limites
smells.summary: Pay special attention to boundaries: we usually get the center of the algorithm right and get the edges wrong.

smells.title: Teste abundantemente bugs próximos
smells.summary: Bugs cluster: when you find one in a function, test it exhaustively; there are probably others.

smells.title: Padrões de falhas são reveladores
smells.summary: Complete, well-ordered test cases expose patterns in the failures that help diagnose the problem.

smells.title: Padrões de cobertura de testes podem ser reveladores
smells.title_en: Test Coverage Patterns Can Be Revealing
smells.summary: Seeing what is or is not executed by the tests gives clues as to why the failing tests are failing.

smells.title: Testes devem ser rápidos
smells.summary: A slow test is not run and is the first to be dropped under pressure; do what you can to keep them fast.
